topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing by introducing the lecturer, the course context, and the lecture's core learning goals.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles of cancer development by examining the interplay between intrinsic replication errors, inherited genetic risk, environmental mutagens, and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how viral and bacterial infections drive malignant transformation through immune suppression, chronic inflammation, and genomic rearrangements, focusing in detail on Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Radiation Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA, including their metabolic activation into reactive electrophilic adducts by xenobiotic pathways.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammatory states, and developmental or tissue-specific contexts foster an environment permissive to tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and assess the carcinogenic risk of various agents.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, summarizing key takeaways and the daily risk-benefit evaluations associated with environmental exposures.
